keyPoints.en: Before colonisation, Malay sultanates had organised government, laws and busy trade; Melaka was a famous entrepôt.
keyPoints.bm: Sebelum dijajah, kesultanan Melayu mempunyai pemerintahan tersusun, undang-undang dan perdagangan sibuk; Melaka ialah entrepot terkenal.

keyPoints.en: Strategic location, monsoon winds and natural wealth (tin, gold, forest products) brought prosperity.
keyPoints.bm: Kedudukan strategik, angin monsun dan kekayaan alam (bijih timah, emas, hasil hutan) membawa kemakmuran.

keyPoints.en: Motives: Gold, Glory, Gospel (wealth, power, religion); the spice trade.
keyPoints.bm: Motif: Gold, Glory, Gospel (kekayaan, kuasa, agama); perdagangan rempah.

keyPoints.en: After the Industrial Revolution: raw materials (tin, later rubber) and markets.
keyPoints.bm: Selepas Revolusi Perindustrian: bahan mentah (bijih timah, kemudian getah) dan pasaran.

keyPoints.en: Portuguese, Dutch and British competed to control trade and territory.
keyPoints.bm: Portugis, Belanda dan British bersaing menguasai perdagangan dan wilayah.

keyPoints.en: Rivalry divided the Malay world by Western interests (later settled by the London Treaty 1824).
keyPoints.bm: Persaingan membahagikan Alam Melayu mengikut kepentingan Barat (kemudian diselesaikan melalui Perjanjian London 1824).

keyPoints.en: Portuguese: force — Melaka 1511. Dutch: alliance with Johor — Melaka 1641; monopoly treaties.
keyPoints.bm: Portugis: kekerasan — Melaka 1511. Belanda: pakatan dengan Johor — Melaka 1641; perjanjian monopoli.

keyPoints.en: British: diplomacy — Penang 1786 (Francis Light), Singapore 1819 (Raffles, Tengku Hussein).
keyPoints.bm: British: diplomasi — Pulau Pinang 1786 (Francis Light), Singapura 1819 (Raffles, Tengku Hussein).
